name: Gatam
overview: Gatam was a male Edomite figure known as the son of Eliphaz and a chief of Edom. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation with the Edomites and his leadership role as a chief, indicating a position of authority within his people. No additional personal details or notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Gatam appears as a proper name in Scripture without any specified meaning or divine origin. It is simply recorded as the name of this Edomite individual in Genesis 36:11.
familyAndRelationships: Gatam is explicitly identified as the son of Eliphaz, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, Scripture does not record further family relationships for Gatam beyond what is noted in his unique attributes.
scriptureSignificance: Gatam's significance lies in his role within the Edomite lineage as a son of Eliphaz and as a chief of Edom. This highlights his place in the genealogical and tribal leadership structure of the Edomites, contributing to the biblical record of the descendants and rulers of Edom. His mention underscores the historical and tribal organization important to understanding the broader narrative of Edom in Scripture.
